status: Approved by the owner on 2026-11-09, to run on a GitHub Actions runner (dispatch only, .github/workflows/detector-quality.yml), not on Databricks. Code written 2026-11-09 (cdm.detector_quality, scripts/detector_quality.py); nothing has run. The run waits for the champion bundle as a release asset.
plan: docs/BACKLOG.md item 15: staged shifts of known size and start month through the monthly drift test; how many months each takes to detect, and how often the test alarms on months with no shift
staged: every shift here is staged (synthetic): real in-distribution test images altered in a known way. Results are labelled staged everywhere and never mixed with the replay's or a live month's numbers
detector: the shipped serving bundle (registry v1, model_gen v2; three seeds, ensemble Mahalanobis OOD score), scored on CPU like the monthly job, against the same validation baseline (3,210 images); the alert rule unchanged: KS p < 0.01 and PSI >= 0.2 (warning PSI >= 0.1)
pool: the clients' test split (3,262 images), lesion-level, never used to fit the detector

blur.what: Gaussian blur of radius sigma pixels at the model's 224 px input

brightness.what: brightness multiplied by a factor (PIL ImageEnhance.Brightness)

jpeg.what: re-encoded as JPEG at quality q, as a cheaper phone camera or a lossy upload would

age_mix.what: the month's images resampled so the share of patients aged 75 or over (the repo's oldest age band) is p (age_approx from the ISIC metadata; no image is altered). share_shifted does not apply to this shift: p is its size

sequence: 12 synthetic months of 300 images each, drawn without replacement within a month; the shift starts in month 4 and stays; months 1 to 3 are unshifted
repeats: 200 sequences per (shift, size, share); sequence r of cell c is seeded with numpy default_rng([20261109, c, r, 0]) for its month draws and [20261109, c, r, 1] for which images are shifted, so its paired control draws the same months
time_to_detect: the first month at or after month 4 whose test alerts, minus 3 (so detecting in the first shifted month is 1); 'not detected' when no month alerts by month 12; reported as the median and the 10th and 90th percentiles over the repeats, and the share detected
false_alarm_rate: the share of unshifted months (months 1 to 3 of every sequence, and all months of the control cell) that alert, with its 95% Wilson interval. Caveat: every month is drawn from the one pool of 3,262 images, and 12 x 300 = 3,600 exceeds it, so images repeat across a sequence's months and across repeats; the months are not independent, and the interval shows only the spread of re-drawing this pool, not of a new population. The same is reported for the warning
also_measured: the month-level false-alarm rate of the post-replay rule (any of four signals, results/phase3/monthly/post_replay_spec.json) on the unshifted months, since that rule's rate is not measured yet
outputs: results/phase3/detector_quality/results.json (aggregates only), and a README table: shift, size, share, months to detect, share detected, false-alarm rate, each labelled staged
compute: A GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner (free for a public repo; 6-hour job limit, set to 340 minutes), CPU only. Scored once per image and setting: 3,262 pool images x (1 unshifted + 9 image shifts) + the 3,210 baseline images, x 3 networks. The age mix and the control only resample. Phase 3's Databricks timing does not carry over to the runner; the run records its own time in score_meta.json. Earlier text (before approval): about 2.5 CPU hours on Databricks, an estimate.
ask: answered 2026-11-09: the owner approved the run on a GitHub Actions runner, and the shift sizes and 12-month design as specced
control: a size-0 control cell (the same sequences, no image altered) runs alongside every shift, so a detection is read against how often the unshifted test alerts in months 4 to 12 by chance
pool_as_run: Amended 2026-11-09, before any run: the runner cannot read the silver tables, so the owner exports once the public ISIC IDs of silver's labelled client validation and test images (role = 'client', split in ('val', 'test'), label not null; 3,210 and 3,262) to config/detector_quality_ids.csv, and the runner fetches exactly those images from the ISIC Archive by ID. The run fails on any other count or a repeated ID. Each image's 224 px model input (the exact Resize and CenterCrop of cdm.data.eval_transform, checked by a test) is kept as a lossless PNG; full-size files would not fit on the runner. These inputs are made from the archive's original files, not from silver's stored copies (re-encoded as JPEG at quality 95 with a 384 px shorter side), so the runner's scores are not the monthly job's scores for the same images; baseline and pool are rescored the same way, so the comparison stays like for like. The baseline is rescored on the runner with the same bundle, not read from gold_drift_baseline. Images of unknown age are left out of age-mixed months
features_for_post_replay_rule: the three networks' 1280-d penultimate features, concatenated (3,840-d), for the embedding signal; PCA fitted on the baseline only
control_as_run: Clarified 2026-11-09, before any run: every sequence of every shift cell has a paired control, the same seed (so the same images every month) with no image altered, and each cell reports its paired controls' alert rate in months 4 to 12 beside its detection. One shared no-shift control cell (its own seeds) gives the false-alarm rate over all 12 months
